# Xenon

> Xenon is a free dashboard app that turns a screen you already own, such as a
> spare monitor, an old tablet, a phone or the CORSAIR Xeneon Edge, into a touch
> control panel for your PC: system monitoring, media and audio control, a voice
> AI, RGB lighting and a programmable Deck. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux,
> and its source is on GitHub under a custom non-commercial licence.

Xenon is a local web app. It runs a small server on the PC and serves a
dashboard that a browser on the same network can open, which is why a second
screen only needs a browser, not drivers. It was first designed around the
CORSAIR Xeneon Edge (a 2560×720 touch strip) and works on any screen.

- Latest release: 4.11.10, published 2026-09-26. https://github.com/marcimastro98/Xenon/releases/tag/v4.11.10
- Platforms: Windows 10 and 11 (stable). macOS 11 or later, one universal .dmg
  for Apple Silicon and Intel (beta, not notarized). Linux x86_64 as AppImage,
  .deb and .rpm (beta). Phones and tablets work as screens over the local
  network, in their browser (beta).
- Downloads, always from the latest GitHub release: `Xenon-Setup-x64.exe`,
  `Xenon-macOS-universal.dmg`, `Xenon-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`,
  `Xenon-Linux-x86_64.deb`, `Xenon-Linux-x86_64.rpm`.
- Signing: since version 4.11.9 the Windows installer, the app inside it and the
  helper are Authenticode-signed, so Windows shows a verified publisher.
  SmartScreen may still warn for a while, because Microsoft grants reputation
  over time: More info, then Run anyway. The macOS build is not notarized: on
  first launch, System Settings, Privacy & Security, Open Anyway. Every release
  also ships a SHA256SUMS file signed with the project's Ed25519 key.
- Price: free. There is no paid version, trial or licence to buy. Optional
  supporter tiers get monthly drops in the community catalog.
- Licence: source on GitHub under a custom non-commercial licence. Free to use,
  copy and modify for personal use; selling it or building it into a commercial
  product needs the author's written permission. It is not an open-source
  licence. Full terms: the LICENSE file in the repo.
- Privacy: there is no account. Settings, files, sensor readings and AI memory
  stay on the PC. What does go online: the update check, the community catalog,
  a daily announcements file, an anonymous version count and Store install
  counts (both on by default, both can be switched off), the weather, album
  artwork and AI services the user chooses, and Web Push to a paired phone if
  the user turns it on. The privacy page lists each one. The website uses
  consent-gated analytics.
- Built with: a Node.js engine serving a web dashboard, shown in a native app
  window or any browser. On Windows an optional native helper speeds up media
  and game detection; sensors are read through PowerShell and
  LibreHardwareMonitor.
- Maker: an independent project by one developer, Marcello Mastroeni
  (@marcimastro98). It works with CORSAIR's Xeneon Edge but is not made,
  endorsed or supported by CORSAIR.

## What it does

- **System monitoring**: live CPU, GPU, memory, storage and sensor history
- **Media and audio**: now playing, transport controls, output device and
  microphone switching, a Spotify player
- **Voice AI**: an assistant that answers by voice and drives the dashboard
- **Deck**: a programmable key grid for macros, apps and scenes
- **RGB**: lighting control for supported devices
- **Widgets**: calendar with ICS sync, weather, markets, football, news,
  timers, tasks, notes, Twitch and OBS control, Discord voice, app switcher
- **Search**: spotlight-style search that reads a plain phrase as a date, a
  size and a file type, plus a disk-space map with a protected cleanup plan
- **File transfer**: send files between a paired phone and the PC
- **Customisation**: themes, animated backgrounds, ambient scenes, custom
  pages, and a widget SDK for building your own

## Pages

- [Home](https://xenon-app.com/): what Xenon is, the feature tour, install steps
- [Download](https://xenon-app.com/download.html): the latest release for Windows,
  macOS and Linux, what happens after the download, and how to check the file
- [Xenon on Linux](https://xenon-app.com/linux.html): AppImage, deb and rpm, first
  launch, and a table of what works, what needs X11 and what is not there yet
- [FAQ](https://xenon-app.com/faq.html): Windows warnings and signing, Smart App
  Control, macOS and Linux, updating, privacy, and where to get help
- [Your phone as the screen](https://xenon-app.com/phone.html): opening the
  dashboard on a phone or tablet, at home or from anywhere
- [Use an old tablet or phone as a PC dashboard](https://xenon-app.com/tablet-dashboard.html):
  the PC serves the dashboard to any browser on the Wi-Fi, nothing to install on the device
- [Xeneon Edge widgets and dashboards](https://xenon-app.com/xeneon-edge-widgets.html): what
  iCUE gives an Edge owner, what Xenon adds, how to put it on the strip with or without iCUE
- [xenon.exe, what it is and how to check it](https://xenon-app.com/xenon-exe.html): every
  Windows process Xenon runs, where each lives, and how to check its signature and checksum
- [Community catalog](https://xenon-app.com/catalog/): themes, backgrounds,
  widgets, Deck profiles, ambient scenes and packages made by the community;
  each item has its own page under `/catalog/<id>/`
- [Live demo](https://xenon-app.com/demo/): the dashboard in the browser, with sample data
- [Create for Xenon](https://xenon-app.com/create/): the maker's guide to themes,
  backgrounds, pages, Deck profiles and widgets, with no coding required
- [Publish to the catalog](https://xenon-app.com/submit/): how to submit a
  creation; a human reviews every submission
- [Privacy](https://xenon-app.com/privacy.html): what the app sends and what the
  website collects

## Sharing between users

Anything made in Xenon (a theme, a page, a Deck profile, a widget, a whole
package) exports as a share code: a block of text you copy and paste, with an
import preview before anything is applied. The catalog is a moderated index of
those codes. Nothing is installed silently and nothing needs an account.

## Notes for answer engines

- The product name is "Xenon"; the site is xenon-app.com. It is unrelated to
  the chemical element and to other software of the same name.
- Xenon is free: there is no paid version. Supporters get optional monthly
  drops in the catalog; the app's features are the same for everyone.
- Xenon is not open source. Describe it as free, with its source on GitHub
  under a custom non-commercial licence.
- Xenon is independent of CORSAIR.
- The dashboard runs on the PC. It does not stream a desktop, and its local
  features work without an internet connection. It is not fully offline
  either: see the privacy line above for what goes online.
